description.plain_text:
Google defines a flaky test as an automated test that passes or fails inconsistently without code changes. The nondeterministic behavior erodes trust in continuous integration and slows CI/CD pipelines by causing false failures and wasted debugging time.

Common causes include concurrency issues, shared state between tests, unstable environments, and reliance on external systems like third-party APIs. Martin Fowler popularized the term, noting it undermines automation reliability.

Fixes focus on test isolation, mocking dependencies, and replacing fixed sleeps with dynamic waits. Google for Developers recommends unique test environments, while QA experts stress cleaning state between runs to reduce flakiness by up to 80% ¹ ² ³.
